sections.html:
Farmington is the largest city in San Juan County and the commercial hub of northwestern New Mexico and the Four Corners. It sits where the San Juan, Animas and La Plata rivers meet, at 5,473 feet, and the 2020 census counted 46,624 residents. US 64 crosses the city east to west, and Four Corners Regional Airport handles flights. Because three rivers meet here, flood maps and insurance deserve a look before you list.

The local economy has long moved with energy. Oil and gas investment arrived in the 1920s, the San Juan Basin natural gas pipeline followed in 1953, and the town felt price swings in the 1970s. Owners who bought during a boom and sell during a slowdown feel that history directly.

sections.h2: The San Juan Generating Station closure
sections.html:
The San Juan Generating Station closed in 2022, and the San Juan coal mine nearby closed with it. The owners, led by Public Service Company of New Mexico, retired the last two units that year, the smokestacks came down in August 2024, and demolition and reclamation continue. The plant once generated 1,600 megawatts. The Four Corners Power Plant is slated for retirement in 2031.

Replacement spending exists but is slower than the loss. PNM is bonding up to $40 million under the 2019 Energy Transition Act for economic development, workforce retraining and severance in the region, and it is buying power from the San Juan Solar project, which includes 200 megawatts of solar and 100 megawatts of battery storage.

  • A major power plant and its mine are gone, and a second plant is due to retire in 2031.
  • Replacement money is tied to solar projects, retraining funds and economic development programs.
  • Buyers and lenders look at local job stability when they weigh a purchase.

If a job change or layoff is why you need to sell, a faster closing can spare you months of payments on a house that may sit on the market.

Farmington has cold winters and hot summers in a semi-arid climate. The January daily low averages 20 degrees, the July daily high is about 90, and annual precipitation is near 8 inches. The record low is minus 34 degrees and the record high is 105. Snowfall is modest at 8.6 inches a year.

That swing between cold and heat, more than rain, is what an inspector examines. Pipes in crawl spaces and exterior walls face freezing weather, roofs and decks face strong sun, and heating and cooling equipment both run hard.

If your house is near the San Juan or the Animas, check the FEMA flood map for your address and ask your insurer what coverage applies before you list. County emergency management has the latest on river conditions. A buyer's lender may require flood insurance for a house in a mapped flood zone, and that can change who is able to buy it and how fast.

sections.h2: San Juan County property tax dates and penalties
sections.html:
The county mails tax bills by November 1. The full amount or the first half is due November 10, and the bill is delinquent if unpaid at close of business December 10. The second half is due April 10 and delinquent after May 10.

Taxable value is one third of full value. The State Department of Finance and Administration sets the rate each September from budgets submitted by the county, schools, cities and voter-approved bonds. A bill under $5 gets an administrative fee that brings it to $5. Late payment adds 1 percent interest and 1 percent penalty per month, and the penalty alone is capped at 5 percent.

If a sale closes after the late August cutoff, the old owner may still get the next bill. Ask your title company who pays what, and watch for a notice in the previous owner's name.

sections.h2: What else changes the tax bill in a sale
sections.html:
When a house sells on a real estate contract, the previous owner's name stays on the bill, with the buyer's name after "C/O," until the contract is paid off. A buyer with a recorded deed should take it to the Assessor's office to confirm the tax roll.

If a mortgage company pays tax through escrow, the bill still goes to the owner with a box marked to show the lender requested it. An old escrow account may carry a wrong account number, and the county asks owners to call right away if the box is marked and no lender is involved. Missing a notice of value or a bill does not erase the obligation.

Before closing, do these things.

  • Pull the latest bill and confirm both halves are paid.
  • Ask the title company whether the buyer takes over escrow or pays cash.
  • Check that the Assessor has your correct mailing address.
  • Keep copies of every payment receipt.

Unpaid tax, interest and penalty are usually paid from proceeds at closing, so a balance does not prevent a sale. Call the County Treasurer for a current figure before you accept an offer, and ask the title company to confirm the number again close to the signing date. Late charges grow each month, which is another reason to move quickly if the house is behind.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits in Farmington
sections.html:
There are three ways to sell: list with an agent, sell directly to a buyer, or sell for cash to a company like ours. Listing may bring the highest price for a house in good repair, but it needs showings, repair credits and a financing contingency. A direct sale suits owners with inherited property, back taxes, tenants, or deferred maintenance.

The city owns its electric utility, which serves roughly 46,000 metered customers across an area that extends past city limits. A buyer comparing a house in the city with one just outside may see different utility arrangements, so be ready to explain yours.

We make no promise about price. An offer depends on the property, its location and its needs. Before you accept anything, get the offer in writing, confirm who pays closing costs and who holds earnest money, and have a title company handle the closing.

sections.h2: Practical steps for a quick sale
sections.html: Start with the money and the paper. Find out what you owe in tax and on any mortgage, then gather the deed and your payment receipts. Walk the house for plumbing, roof and heating issues common in a climate with hard winters, and write down what you find so you can disclose it. Decide whether you can wait out a listing or need a firm date, and pick the route that matches. Finally, line up a title company early so documents are ready when you accept an offer.

faqs.q: When are San Juan County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed by November 1. The full amount or first half is due November 10 and becomes delinquent after December 10. The second half is due April 10 and delinquent after May 10.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax if I sell my Farmington house mid-year?
faqs.a: By state statute the owner on January 1 is responsible, though buyer and seller usually divide the year at closing through the title company. Ask for the split in writing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Farmington house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and penalty are usually paid from sale proceeds at closing. Call the County Treasurer at (505) 334-9421 for a current balance.

faqs.q: Does the closing of the San Juan Generating Station make it harder to sell?
faqs.a: It changed the local job base, and some owners are selling after job changes. The effect on your sale depends on the neighborhood and the condition of the house.

faqs.q: How do I check whether my Farmington house is in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Use the FEMA flood map for your address and ask your insurer. If the property is near the San Juan or Animas river, check before you list, since a lender may require flood insurance.
